metadata.title: Asynchronous Methods for Deep Reinforcement Learning (Mnih et al., 2016)
metadata.framework: Asynchronous multi-threaded RL training with parallel actor-learners, culminating in A3C (Asynchronous Advantage Actor-Critic)
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on arXiv:1602.01783 PDF text.

nodes.name: Asynchronous training framework
nodes.statement: Multiple actor-learner threads run in parallel on a single multi-core CPU, each with its own copy of the environment. Each thread computes gradients locally and asynchronously updates a shared global parameter vector $\theta$, using asynchronous SGD or RMSProp without locks.

nodes.name: Advantage actor-critic
nodes.statement: An actor-critic architecture where the policy $\pi(a_t|s_t; \theta)$ (actor) and value function $V(s_t; \theta_v)$ (critic) share a convolutional neural network body. The policy gradient uses the advantage $A(s_t, a_t) = R_t - V(s_t; \theta_v)$ as baseline, where $R_t = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \gamma^k r_{t+k} + \gamma^n V(s_{t+n}; \theta_v)$ is the $n$-step return.

nodes.name: n-step returns
nodes.statement: Instead of one-step TD, use $n$-step returns: $R_t = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \gamma^k r_{t+k} + \gamma^n V(s_{t+n}; \theta_v)$, which provides a better bias-variance tradeoff and propagates rewards faster. Operates up to $t_{\max}$ steps or until a terminal state.

nodes.name: Entropy regularization
nodes.statement: Add an entropy bonus $H(\pi(s_t; \theta))$ to the policy loss to discourage premature convergence to deterministic policies and encourage exploration. The full loss gradient for the policy includes $\beta \nabla_\theta H(\pi(s_t; \theta))$.

nodes.name: REINFORCE policy gradient (baseline form)
nodes.statement: $\nabla_\theta \log \pi(a_t | s_t; \theta) (R_t - b_t)$ where $b_t$ is a baseline that does not depend on the action. Setting $b_t = V(s_t; \theta_v)$ gives the advantage actor-critic.

nodes.name: A3C algorithm
nodes.statement: Each thread: (1) Sync local parameters $\theta' \leftarrow \theta$ from global. (2) Interact with environment for up to $t_{\max}$ steps using policy $\pi(\cdot; \theta')$, collecting $(s_t, a_t, r_t)$. (3) Compute $n$-step returns $R_t$ and accumulate gradients $d\theta \leftarrow d\theta + \nabla_{\theta'} \log \pi(a_t|s_t; \theta')(R_t - V(s_t; \theta'_v))$ and $d\theta_v \leftarrow d\theta_v + \nabla_{\theta'_v} (R_t - V(s_t; \theta'_v))^2$. (4) Asynchronously update global $\theta, \theta_v$ using accumulated gradients.

nodes.name: Decorrelation via parallelism replaces experience replay
nodes.statement: Multiple parallel actors in different parts of the environment naturally decorrelate their experiences, providing a complementary stabilization mechanism to experience replay (used in DQN). This enables on-policy methods like actor-critic and SARSA to be trained stably with neural networks.

nodes.name: Four asynchronous methods presented
nodes.statement: The paper presents asynchronous variants of four RL algorithms: one-step Q-learning, one-step SARSA, n-step Q-learning, and advantage actor-critic (A3C). A3C achieves the best performance while being the most general.

nodes.name: CPU training competitive with GPU
nodes.statement: A3C on a single multi-core CPU (16 threads) trains faster and achieves better results than DQN on a GPU, while using far less memory (no experience replay buffer). A3C achieves superhuman performance on many Atari games and solves continuous control tasks.
